title: The base of a red gate is measured like any gate
description: On a paid measurement (P128.38, two (iii) runs) the drive's inline base measurement (run-test-gate.py --base-of, bounded by BASE_MEASURE_SECONDS = the 120 s foreground bound) was torn down, recorded not-knowable, and the drive then took the no-base path and resumed the writer twice over a red the base reproduces case for case. The base measurement is the one gate the drive still runs inline past the one background rule.
desiredOutcome: A red task gate whose base run outlives the Bash foreground bound is measured in the background and stops as gate-red-base when the base reproduces it, with no writer session resumed; a base that cannot be known stops the drive with its own answer

tasks.title: A red gate's base is measured in the background under the one gate rule, and an unknowable base stops the drive instead of resuming the writer
tasks.description:
plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py measures a red task gate's base inline: base_reading_for -> measure_base -> _base_in runs run-test-gate.py --base-of <runId> --record in a detached tree under run_verb_bounded(..., BASE_MEASURE_SECONDS) (around line 2780-2930). When that run outlives 120 s it is torn down and recorded verdict not-knowable, and gate_red_decision then treats the red as introduced and returns gate-red-writer (resume) - so a red the base reproduces spends writer rounds and the run stops at round 2/2. Observed on P128.38: the failing suite's base run under a sandbox takes longer than 120 s; the one failing case fails at the base, case for case.

REQUIRED, as one rule rather than a special case:
1. The base measurement is a drive gate step like the task gate: it goes through gate_in_background's decision (always a step of its own under auto; unmeasured or past the foreground bound -> background; measured under the bound -> may stay inline), is launched as a dispatch with a self-contained run: command (build the detached tree at the red run's head, run run-test-gate.py --base-of --record with no 120 s cut, tear the tree down through remove_base_tree, record the reading on the start's baseMeasured mark), waited on, and decided from what it recorded - the same launch/wait/read-back shape as launch_gate / background_gate / gate_wait_said. Reuse those helpers or factor a shared one; do not write a second copy of the launch-wait-readback machinery. The kill safety the inline path has (mark before the run naming the tree and pids, sweep_base_trees removing a killed run's tree) must hold for the background run too.
2. A base reading that is not knowable (the base run produced no row, failed, or was really cut) must NOT fall through to gate-red-writer or spend a writer round. It stops as a distinct decision (name it e.g. gate-red-base-unknown) whose options are rerun (measure the gate again), measure-base (measure the base again, clearing the start's mark) and block (with --reason); add it to DECISIONS, the step text table, the decision kind map, --explain and every table the drive's own lints hold decisions to. no-base (no comparable base run and none measurable because HEAD moved) keeps its current meaning unless the same reasoning applies - state the choice in the outcome.
3. drive-phase.py auto (the prompt hook's driver) must run the new step without a model, as it runs dispatch-gate/wait-gate today.
4. Prose that describes the base measurement must say the new behaviour: plugins/audit/reference/execute-task.md (the recorded-gate step, around line 265), plugins/audit/reference/orchestrator.md (around line 16-19), PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (around lines 4907 and 4957), and the comment block above BASE_MEASURE_VERDICTS. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

CASES (tests/test_drive_phase.py; tests/test_drive_without_model.py if auto is touched):
- the k15n shape: a red task gate, a base run that outlives the foreground bound (simulate with a stub run-test-gate whose --base-of sleeps past a shortened bound or reports a long recorded mean - do not sleep 120 s in a suite), the base reproduces every failing case -> the drive dispatches the base measurement to the background, reads it back, and decides gate-red-base; no gate-red-writer, no resume, writer resumes counter unchanged.
- a base that cannot be known -> the new stop decision with options rerun/measure-base/block, and no writer round spent.
- measure-base clears the mark and measures again; a killed background base run leaves a tree that the next drive sweeps.
- under auto the base step runs without a model.
Prove each red-first: mutate the fix (e.g. route not-knowable back to gate-red-writer; restore the inline bounded call), assert the mutation landed, and show the case goes red; restore in the same command. Purge __pycache__ between mutate/restore.

DEPENDANTS (owe a check, each named in the outcome): tests/test_drive_phase.py, tests/test_drive_without_model.py (auto's step table), tests/test_run_test_gate.py and tests/test__evidence_io.py if --base-of or base_run change, tests/test__impact.py (reads drive-phase decision tables), tools/_suite.py, the decision tables gate-parity / lints hold to SECURITY.md and docs, plugins/audit/scripts/governance/run-test-gate.py (--base-of contract).

tasks.title: The background base run and next never lose each other's state, and the gate verdict after a base run is read back, never measured again inline
tasks.description:
The phase review of P161.1 (e4e4e4f6) found these in plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py. Fix the class, not each instance.

MED 1. base-run (the background base measurement) and next both read-modify-write the one drive state file. base-run takes no lock (fresh_keeper, near line 3011). next reads the state once at drive() (near line 10918) and writes its copy back repeatedly: take_lock, sweep_base_trees, drive_locked, give_back_lock. A next during a running base-run is the normal case under wait-base and in waves, and it overwrites base-run's done/reading. cut_short then reads that as unknowable and gives a false gate-red-base-unknown. Or the lost ran=True makes base_waiting loop and start a second base run. Required: base-run writes its progress and result only to a file of its own per launch under the drive's state dir (keyed by task and launch), written atomically. next folds that file into the mark when it reads. No process but next writes the shared state file. Remove the comment that accepts the lost write.

MED 2. write_state (near line 1309) opens the file with "w" and dumps into it, which is not atomic. Make every state write atomic: a temp file in the same directory, then os.replace. Move started(proc.pid) (near line 1189) inside run_verb_bounded's try, so a raising callback still tears the group down. The started callback must report a state failure, not raise.

MED 3. base_gate (near line 3143) gets the red verdict back after a base run by calling task_gate/record_gate directly. When the red row cannot be repeated (a timed-out row, a rerun mark that adds --no-reuse, a changed tree), the whole slow gate runs inline and unbounded inside next, which is the shape this phase removes. Record the red run's id and status on the base mark at launch, and read the verdict back through read_back (unrepeatable_red for a row no repeat may copy), the same path background_gate uses.

LOW, same change:
(a) A mark the previous version wrote for a cut base ({verdict: not-knowable, run: None}, with no ran/background key) must read as unknowable, not fall to gate-red-writer.
(b) Apply a mark's reading only to the red run it was measured for (held['of'] equals the row's run or the run it repeats). Otherwise it is unknowable.
(c) gate-red-base-unknown's rule text names the owner's commit-task-work.py --override-verdict route, as gate-red-base does, and offers resume and retry as answers that are never recommended. A base that can never be measured must not be a dead end for a real regression. Nothing is sent without an explicit answer.

Cases for each, red-first: mutate the fix, assert the mutation landed, see the case go red, and restore in the same command. Purge __pycache__ between cycles. Simulate interleaving deterministically, by calling base-run's writer and next's read/write in a chosen order, not with sleeps. Dependants: tests/test_drive_without_model.py (auto runs base-run), tests/test__worktrees.py, and the prose in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md and execute-task.md that describes the base run and the unknown stop. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: A red in a derived gate step has its base measured through the failing suites it names, and a step that cannot be re-run is no-base, not an unknown stop
tasks.description:
A red in a step the gate derives (affected/related, affected/python and the like) cannot have its base measured: run-test-gate.py --base-of runs only the red steps whose command the row keeps verbatim (base_commands, near line 5209), and a derived step's row keeps digests only. So --base-of exits 2 "nothing to run at its base". Since P161.1 the drive reads that as an unknowable base and stops as gate-red-base-unknown. Before that it sent the red to the writer as no-base. Either way the question "does the base fail the same cases" goes unanswered for every derived step, which is where most task-gate reds land. It is the same class as a cut base run.

REQUIRED, one rule:
1. --base-of measures a derived red step at the base by running the failing suites that step's row names (its failing cases are per suite path), with the command the runner derives for those suites the way the gate itself derives it. Reuse the derivation run-test-gate uses for affected steps (_affected, _suite_at_base, base_red); do not write a second spelling of the runner command. The base row then reads like any other base run, and base_red compares case by case.
2. Where a derived step's base genuinely cannot be re-run (no failing suite named, a runner with no per-suite command), --base-of says so per step in its JSON answer (notRun with the reason). The drive then treats that step's base as no-base, structurally unmeasurable like a moved HEAD: the red goes to the writer as it did before P161. It is not the unknown stop, which stays for a base run that was started and was cut, killed, or left no row. State the choice in the code comment above the decision.
3. Cases (tests/test_run_test_gate.py, tests/test_drive_phase.py): a red affected step whose failing suite fails the same case at base gives gate-red-base with no writer round; a red affected step whose suite is green at base goes to the writer; a derived step that cannot be re-run gives no-base and goes to the writer, not gate-red-base-unknown. Red-first for each: mutate the fix, assert the mutation landed, and restore in the same command. Purge __pycache__.

Dependants: tests/test__evidence_io.py, tests/test__affected.py (if present), tests/test_drive_without_model.py, and the prose in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md and plugins/audit/reference/execute-task.md that describes --base-of and the unknown stop. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

outcome.technical: run-test-gate.py: base_commands(row, manifest, phase_id, tree) now returns (commands, published, left). A red step whose row keeps its command verbatim runs as recorded (and stays published). A red DERIVED step goes through the new _derived_at_base: its arm is read off the name, its suites are _ev.named_failing_suites([step]) (the suites its failing cases are recorded under), and the command comes from _affected.entries_for([{path, arm}], phase, meta, tree), the same derivation affected_steps/steps_for use, so the runner command is not spelled a second time. Derived commands stay unpublished, so the row keeps a digest as the task run did; _record_base_run now takes the published list. A step that cannot be re-run goes into left as {name, reason}. Reasons: arm not in _affected.ARMS, runner named no failing suite, entries_for's widen reason (no path-scoped spelling), no command spelled, declared step kept as a digest. _run_base_of passes row.phaseId or args.phase. When nothing can run, --json now prints the answer shape (steps [], notRun with reasons, baseRed null, runId null) and exits E_ASK as before; the text form names each step with its reason. notRun is now a list of {name, reason} instead of a list of names. git grep found no other reader of notRun or base_commands. drive-phase.py: new base_unrunnable(answer) returns the joined reasons only when the answer ran nothing (steps == []) and every red step is in notRun. _base_in returns a fourth value, measurable, which is False only on that answer. measure_base passes it through, so take_base marks measurable False and unknowable False, the row's no-base reading stands, and base_reading_for sends the red to the writer (gate-red-writer) and not to gate-red-base-unknown. That stop is kept for a base run that was cut, killed, failed or left no reading. The choice is stated in the section comment ("A BASE NO COMMAND CAN RUN IS NOT A BASE NOBODY KNOWS") and in a comment above the decision in _base_in. Docs: run-test-gate.py's --base-of section comment, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (the run-test-gate --base-of paragraph and the drive-phase unknown-stop paragraph) and execute-task.md step 3 now describe a derived step's base being measured, notRun, and an unrunnable base going to the writer. M2 (base_unrunnable always None) turned bdr3 red with gate-red-base-unknown. M2b, the over-fire direction (any notRun read as unrunnable), turned bdr1 and bdr2 red. M3 (no JSON when nothing runs) turned bod3 red. Before the fix, bod1-bod3 failed by assertion with exit 2 'digests only', bod4 raised TypeError on the old signature, and bdr1-bdr3 were red. Sweeps: the three named suites exit 0 ('3/3 files ok, 1645 cases'). The lint and dependant suites test__deps, test__output_lints, test__refs, test__evidence_io and test__affected_tests exit 0 ('5/5 files ok, 1144 cases'). house_style_violations returned [], prose_number_claims and doc_prose_numbers report nothing in the changed files, and measure-context --gate exits 0 (GATE OK). tasks.title: A base-run claim left by a dead holder is taken over, so a killed base run never wedges the drive
tasks.description:
A verification review of c78c89c5 found a med regression in the exclusive claim on a base-run launch (plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py claim_launch near lines 3212-3234, the refusal in base_run near 3437-3444, base_waiting near 3046-3052).

claim_launch creates the .claim file before anything records that the run started: ran=True is written only by take_base's first keep, after the ledger read. Nothing checks whether the pid in the claim is alive, and only drop_progress removes the claim. If base-run dies between the claim and ran (Esc under auto tears the group down, a kill, or an exception after the claim file is created), what is left is a claim with a dead pid, no progress record, and a mark with background set and ran False. Every later next prints wait-base with the same run: line, every relaunch is refused with E_USAGE ("pid N holds its claim"), and measure-base cannot be answered, because nothing is pending during a wait. The drive is stuck until someone deletes the claim by hand. Before c78c89c5, relaunching the run: line was how a wait recovered.

Required: a claim whose holder is not alive (_locks.pid_alive answers False, read through the shared liveness rule, so a refused ps keeps its third answer and never counts as dead) is taken over by the next base-run. Remove it and create it again exclusively, then measure. A claim with no readable pid that is older than a short grace counts as abandoned in the same way. Two live base-runs still get exactly one claim. Cases, red-first: a claimant killed before ran, so the relaunch takes the claim over and measures; a live claimant, so the second run is refused; an unreadable claim. Mutate the fix, assert the mutation landed, see the case go red, and restore in the same command. Purge __pycache__. No F/P/BUG ids in comments. The commit's claims block must say what the cases prove; the previous one wrongly said no case was added.

add: tests/test_drive_phase.py: a claim whose holder died before ran is taken over by the relaunch, which measures; a live claimant still refuses a second run; an unreadable claim past the grace is taken over

outcome.technical: WHAT CHANGED, BY FILE, AND WHY IT IS HERE. (1) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py, the task's subject: BASE_CLAIM_SUFFIX and claim_launch's O_EXCL file are removed. claim_launch(ctx, name) is _locks.acquire(project, 'base-<phase>.<task>.<launch>', wait=0, per_call=True, reclaim=True), refusing with the library's own lines. base_run takes the claim, reads the mark again under it (new measure_launch: refuses a replaced launch or one that already ran), and gives the claim back in `finally` (release_launch), adding a WARNING if the release is refused because it was taken over. base_lock_name derives the name from the record's basename. drop_progress(ctx, path) also releases the launch's lock through _locks.release, which refuses a claim recording another process that still runs. (2) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_locks.py, where the note puts the primitive: BASE_PREFIX, a `base-<ascii id>` name shape in is_plugin_name/name_refusal, and acquire(reclaim=True). reclaim takes over a claim judge() reads as not live, in the call that judged it, through the stamped _take_over, and refuses a live one as the default does. (3) plugins/audit/scripts/usage/audit-usage.py, from note 3: acquire_lock's E_STALE-then-takeover=True retake is now one acquire(..., reclaim=True). Its docstring was corrected: it claimed the two-step refused a run that took the name in between, but the second call judged again and took over whatever it found. (4) tests/test_drive_phase.py: the new lc-block (lc1-lc7). Each case uses a real child process running base_run that either dies with os._exit after the claim and before `ran`, or holds until released. The block also has an AST scan of drive-phase.py's source (hand_rolled_claims) and its twin. bi13 now runs in a git-initialised world (_bk_world), because a lock lives in the clone's git dir. (5) tests/test__locks.py: the new rc-block, rc1-rc4: reclaim against a gone holder (twin: the default still answers E_STALE), a live holder, an unreadable claim young and aged, and base- name validity, with user-base-* refused. (6) tests/test_audit_usage.py: ur1. It wraps _locks.acquire and _locks.judge for one acquire_lock call and plants a live winner in each window: after an acquire answers E_STALE, and after judge reads the holder dead inside the retaking call. The winner must never be displaced. (7) tests/test__output_lints.py: lk4 read every caller of `_locks.acquire(` as text and flagged any line holding `isinstance(` and `code`. Once the driver called acquire, that flagged six unrelated driver lines, so the scan now reads the AST through _acquire_misreads: names bound to an acquire(...) result that are then tested with isinstance. lk4b is its twin. (8) PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: the drive-phase section's claim paragraph now describes the _locks claim, its takeover and the lc cases. (9) SECURITY.md, plugins/audit/commands/worktree.md and plugins/audit/scripts/governance/audit-lock.py (docstring only): each lists the plugin's lock names, and base-<id> is now one. (10) plugins/audit/reference/orchestrator.md: 'Every lock this script can take' became 'Every lock you take', because audit-lock.py now accepts base-<id>, which the list does not name. I did not add a paragraph because the file is at its measure-context ceiling: 61987 / 62000 now, under `measure-context.py --gate` exit 0. LIVENESS IS THE LIBRARY'S: _locks.liveness/judge decide; a refused ps reads 'unverified' and counts as live; an unparseable claim counts as live until STALE_MINUTES; an empty claim is taken over at once. No other hand-rolled exclusion exists in the P161 diff: base_running reads _locks.pid_alive, which is a liveness read, not an exclusion. HOW EDITS WERE MADE: early shell-heredoc edits to audit-lock.py, SECURITY.md and worktree.md drew a bash-write-guard notice. I restored those three files with git checkout (the diff was only mine, checked by --stat) and redid them with Edit, which the plan gate allowed. Later _locks.py edits were shell-written after an allowed Edit on that file. Every file is inside the widened scope.

tasks.description:
A verification review of 3d8f2128 found the following.

MED 1. plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_locks.py, the takeover loop in acquire (read_lock near line 1474, the stamp near line 1511, reached by reclaim near line 1566). Each pass reads the claim and only afterwards stamps the file. judge rules on the old contents, and _take_over checks against the newer stamp. Two reclaimers racing over a dead claim: B stamps, reclaims and links its live claim; A then stamps B's file, still judges the dead contents it read, its stamp matches, and it unlinks B's live claim. Both base runs measure, and with audit-usage two backfills both write the ledger. Required: the stamp handed to _take_over must belong to the bytes that were judged. Stamp before read_lock, re-stamp after the read, and re-read on a mismatch. A red-first case in tests/test__locks.py plants a winner between A's read and A's stamp and asserts A is refused and B keeps the claim.

LOW 2. drive-phase.py base_run's finally (near line 3471): no case fails if release_launch is missing. Assert that the base- lock file is absent from _locks.lock_dir after a run that measured, a run that was refused, and a measure_launch stubbed to raise.

LOW 3. A claim left by a run killed before it recorded ran is cleared only when the same launch runs again. measure-base mints a new launch, so the old base- claim stays in the lock directory forever, and /audit:doctor warns about it with advice that does not fit (_doctor_hygiene.py near line 355, abandoned_advice). Required: when a new launch replaces a background mark, release the replaced launch's base- claim (release still refuses a live holder). Give abandoned_advice a base- branch that says the next base-run of that launch reclaims it, and otherwise it may be deleted. Add a case for each.

tasks.title: A takeover removes only the claim it judged, atomically, and every base-run claim is released once nothing names its launch
tasks.description:
A verification review of bfc818b2 found the following.

MED 1. plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_locks.py _take_over (near lines 1077-1079): the removal is "stat the file, check the stamp, unlink the path", and nothing makes the check and the unlink one step. Two reclaimers judging the same dead claim A: R1's check passes and it is paused; R2 checks, unlinks A and links its live claim B; R1 resumes and unlinks B. Both believe they hold the claim. A human --takeover goes through the same lines. The takeover race is now a recurring class: each round closed one window of a multi-step check-then-act on claim files. Fix it with an invariant. tasks.title: A filesystem that refuses the kernel lock keeps every lock working, with one errno reading shared by both lock users
tasks.description:
A verification review of e8a0d4bc (the lock-directory mutex) found the following.

MED 1. plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_locks.py _try_lock / _dir_mutex (near lines 976-1038): only contention errnos count as "held". Any other errno from the lock call (ENOLCK on NFS with lockd down, EOPNOTSUPP/ENOTSUP on a FUSE or SMB mount) is re-raised, so acquire answers E_ERR, every manifest-mutating command and panel write refuses, and release and takeover fail. Before e8a0d4bc the link/O_EXCL claim worked there. Required: classify a lock-call errno in ONE place shared with plugins/audit/scripts/usage/usage_ledger.py (its _try_lock/_CONTENDED/LOCK_UNAVAILABLE classification), not in two copies that disagree. A filesystem that refuses the kernel lock proceeds without the mutex (the pre-mutex behaviour) and says so in the answer's basis. Contention still waits up to the bound. Cases: a fake flock raising ENOLCK and EOPNOTSUPP, where acquire and release still work and the answer names the missing mutex; and usage_ledger reads the same classification.

LOW 2. tests/test__locks.py race cases (near lines 1046-1136): the 2 s bound starts when .r2in is written, before the second racer's acquire. Under load the unprotected second racer can miss it, and mx5/mx6/mx7 then pass with no mutex. Have the second racer write .r2at when it reaches the critical section (wrap _take_over or _dir_mutex in _MX_CHILD), start the bound from it, and make mx6 require .r2at.

LOW 3. _locks.py (near lines 1023-1024): .mutex is opened O_RDWR|O_CREAT with 0o644, which breaks a clone shared by two OS users (EACCES, then E_ERR). flock works on a read-only descriptor and Windows locking needs read access only: open with O_RDONLY|O_CREAT, create with 0o666 so the umask decides, and add a case.

Red-first for every new case: mutate the fix, assert the mutation landed, see the case go red, and restore in the same command. Purge __pycache__. No F/P/BUG ids in comments. The SECURITY.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md lock sentences state the degraded mode.
